# Copilot instructions

Owner: greenblacked (Serhii). These apply to Copilot Chat, code review and the coding agent.

`AGENTS.md` is the single set of rules for this repository and `CONTRIBUTING.md` covers branch,
commit and naming mechanics. Read both before changing anything. Where they differ from the
generic rules below, the repository's own files win. Do not restate or paraphrase them from memory.

## Repository gates

This repository is Markdown and configuration for agent skills; the only code is `skillcheck`.
Run all of these before finishing a change (CI runs the same):

- `make validate` (every skill, subagent and the marketplace manifest, strict)
- `make catalogue` (listing ceilings, README and `docs/ci.md` against the tree, workflows, shell, hook, providers)
- `make test` (the validator's own tests; needs `python -m pip install pytest pytest-xdist pytest-cov`)
- `make naming` and `make attribution` (branch name, commit subjects, file names, tool attribution)
- `make lint` (ruff, markdownlint, yamllint, actionlint, codespell, for whichever are installed)

A skill change needs its `evals/trigger-eval.json` and a README row. Never edit a skill's
`description` just to make a check pass, never turn a validator error into a warning, and
add a line under `## [Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` for any change worth a release note.
No emoji other than the three severity markers in `AGENTS.md`'s Review guidelines, no
exclamation marks, no secrets.

## Serhii's standing rules

- Never add tooling attribution anywhere published: no "Generated by/with" footers, no
  `Co-authored-by` trailer for Copilot or any AI tool, no session links, no model names in
  commits, PR titles or bodies, issues, comments, code or docs.
- Never use a tool-named branch prefix (`copilot/`, `claude/`, `codex/`, `ai/`, `bot/`). If the
  coding agent forces one on its branch or trailers, flag it in the PR instead of claiming
  compliance. After a PR is created, re-read its body and remove any appended footer.
- Branches are `<type>/<short-kebab>`, type one of `feat`, `fix`, `chore`, `docs`, `ci`, `test`
  (enforced by `scripts/check_naming.py`; `refactor`, `perf` and `build` from the generic list are
  rejected here). `fb/` is retired. `CONTRIBUTING.md` has the length guidance.
- Branch from and open pull requests into `dev` (flow `dev` -> `stage` -> `main`); the
  "branch from `main`" line in `CONTRIBUTING.md` predates this.
- Commits are authored by `greenblacked <23718180+greenblacked@users.noreply.github.com>`,
  one logical change each, imperative, subject at most 72 characters. This repository's subject
  format (capital letter, no `feat:`/`docs:` type prefix) is set in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and wins here.
- One change per pull request. Review your own diff adversarially (bugs, edge cases, security,
  missing tests, docs) before asking for review.
- Never push unreviewed or unverified work, not even to get a PR open sooner; every commit
  pushed must already pass the gates above.
- Never merge without Serhii's explicit go-ahead. Never force-push or rewrite pushed history.
- Merge only when every check on the PR head is green and the target branch's latest push CI
  run is completed and green. Nothing red, pending or queued. One merge at a time, waiting for
  the target's CI after each. Tell Serhii about branches to delete.
- Codex gate: wait until Codex has finished both its Security Review and Code Review on the
  PR's current head (a new push restarts the wait). Fix or answer every comment and resolve every
  review thread before merging; zero unresolved threads.
- Catalogue site (cross-device): a change to the catalogue site or its build scripts
  (`scripts/build_catalogue_site.py`, `site_style.py`) is a UI change for every phone and tablet
  browser, not the one it was reported on: Android Chrome, iOS Safari old and new, all three
  backgrounds. Use feature detection with a graceful fallback, add regression tests that fail
  first, and run `make test-browser` locally.
- Never put secrets, tokens or `.env` contents in code, commits, PRs or docs; if you find one,
  report only its path.

## Copilot-specific files

- `.github/instructions/` holds path-scoped instructions: `agents`, `skills`, `validator` and
  `workflows` mirror `.claude/rules/`, and `review` mirrors `REVIEW.md`. Review a pull request against
  `review.instructions.md` and `AGENTS.md`'s Review guidelines.
- `.github/agents/` holds the custom agents `explorer`, `investigator`, `implementer` and
  `reviewer`, mirroring `.claude/agents/`. `.github/prompts/` holds `ship`, `verify`,
  `scaffold-skill`, `eval-skill`, `skill-doctor` and `skill-gap`, mirroring `.claude/commands/`.
  Prompt files are for the IDE.
- Each of those opens with `<!-- source: <path> sha256: <hash> -->`. `make catalogue` runs
  `scripts/check_copilot.py`, which fails when a source has no wrapper or changed after its
  wrapper was written. After editing a source, carry the change across and update the hash;
  `python3 scripts/check_copilot.py --help` has the steps. The source file is the full rules.
- Prompts carry the full procedure, so they can run on their own; instructions and agents are thin.
- The plugins' skills are not duplicated for Copilot; install the plugins.
